sec: Distal vs proximal RTA table, row by row · p823

items.q: Match the two RTA columns to the table rows — 1) Kidney stones  2) Urine pH  3) Glycosuria … A) Absent (proximal RTA)  B) Present (distal RTA)  C) Alkaline (distal RTA)
items.exp: Distal RTA: kidney stones present, urine pH alkaline, glycosuria absent. Proximal RTA reverses all three. (Book p823)

items.q: In proximal RTA the urine pH is best described as:
opts: Normal, because the distal acidification machinery is intact
Alkaline, because bicarbonate leaks distally
Fixed at 5.0 whatever the systemic pH
Excluded from the comparison table
items.exp: Proximal RTA has a normal urine pH whereas distal RTA has an alkaline urine pH. (Book p823)

items.q: Rickets in distal RTA is due to ______, while in proximal RTA it is due to ______.
opts: Ca²⁺ resorption; loss of phosphorus
loss of phosphorus; Ca²⁺ resorption
loss of phosphorus; loss of phosphorus
hypercalciuria; hypocalciuria
items.exp: Table row ‘Rickets’: distal RTA — due to (D/t) Ca²⁺ resorption; proximal RTA — due to loss of phosphorus. (Book p823)

items.q: A patient with RTA has rickets and NO kidney stones but does pass glucose in urine with normal blood sugar. Which column of the table is this?
opts: Proximal RTA — glycosuria present, stones absent
Distal RTA — glycosuria present, stones absent
Proximal RTA — glycosuria absent, stones present
Distal RTA — glycosuria absent, stones absent
items.exp: Glycosuria with absent kidney stones identifies the proximal RTA column of the table. (Book p823)

items.q: Match the inherited causes row — 1) Distal RTA  2) Proximal RTA  3) Mode of distal inheritance … A) Fanconi's syndrome  B) Autosomal recessive  C) H⁺ ATPase / H⁺ K⁺ ATPase defect
items.exp: Inherited row: distal RTA — autosomal recessive H⁺ ATPase / H⁺ K⁺ ATPase defect; proximal RTA — Fanconi's syndrome. (Book p823)

items.q: The acquired cause listed for distal RTA is ______ and for proximal RTA is ______.
opts: Sjögren's syndrome; myeloma
myeloma; Sjögren's syndrome
Sjögren's syndrome; Sjögren's syndrome
myeloma; tenofovir only
items.exp: Acquired row of the table: distal RTA — Sjögren's syndrome; proximal RTA — myeloma. (Book p823)

items.q: Match each item to the RTA type it belongs to — 1) Sjögren's syndrome  2) Myeloma  3) Fanconi's syndrome  4) Autosomal recessive H⁺ ATPase defect … A) Proximal RTA acquired  B) Distal RTA inherited  C) Distal RTA acquired  D) Proximal RTA inherited
items.exp: Sjögren's = distal acquired; myeloma = proximal acquired; Fanconi's syndrome = proximal inherited; AR H⁺ ATPase/H⁺ K⁺ ATPase defect = distal inherited. (Book p823)

items.q: ‘Kidney stones are present in distal RTA but absent in proximal RTA, while glycosuria behaves the opposite way.’
opts: True — stones present/absent and glycosuria absent/present respectively
False — stones are present in both types
False — glycosuria is present in both types
True, except that stones are also present in proximal RTA
items.exp: The table prints stones Present (distal) / Absent (proximal) and glycosuria Absent (distal) / Present (proximal). (Book p823)

items.q: Two patients both have NAGMA. One has severe hypokalemia with an alkaline urine; the other has mild hypokalemia with a normal urine pH. Which is which?
opts: First is distal RTA, second is proximal RTA
First is proximal RTA, second is distal RTA
Both are distal RTA, differing only in severity
Both are proximal RTA; urine pH is unrelated
items.exp: Severe NAGMA with hypokalemia and an alkaline urine = distal RTA; mild NAGMA with hypokalemia and a normal urine pH = proximal RTA. (Book p823)

items.q: All but one of these are correctly paired in the distal vs proximal RTA table. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Kidney stones — absent in distal RTA
Urine pH — alkaline in distal RTA
NAGMA with hypokalemia — severe in distal RTA
Glycosuria — absent in distal RTA
items.exp: Kidney stones are *present* in distal RTA and absent in proximal RTA; the other three pairings are as printed. (Book p823)

items.q: Which single table row best separates distal from proximal RTA at the bedside?
opts: Urine pH — alkaline in distal RTA versus normal in proximal RTA
Serum potassium — always normal in distal RTA
Serum bicarbonate — always normal in proximal RTA
Anion gap — raised in distal RTA only
items.exp: Both types show NAGMA, so the discriminating rows are urine pH (alkaline vs normal), stones (present vs absent) and glycosuria (absent vs present). (Book p823)
